author: Matthew Neschis
title: John Harbaugh makes swift U-turn after bolting back to Baltimore following Giants meeting - NewsBreak
text:
By Matthew Neschis ,
2 hours ago The New York Giants won't have to wait with bated breath on John Harbaugh’s decision any longer after the highly sought-after head coach reportedly agreed to come to the Big Apple.
The NFL world was stunned last Tuesday when the Ravens revealed they were parting ways with Harbaugh following an 18-year run as the team's head coach. Since his departure from Baltimore, He has attracted considerable attention — with ESPN's Adam Schefter revealing that his agent, Bryan Harlan, received inquiries from seven teams within just 45 minutes of the announcement.
Among those interested in acquiring Harbaugh’s talents are the Giants, who had the opening swing at him during his first in-person interview. Despite reports suggesting there was a chance the 63-year-old “does not leave the building,” he initially departed New York without signing a new deal.

According to The Athletic’s Ian O'Connor, Harbaugh visited the Giants at their team facility in East Rutherford, New Jersey and went to a subsequent dinner with several of the organization’s top brass.
Yet by the time Harbaugh arrived at Teterboro Airport and boarded his flight back to Baltimore on Wednesday night, he still wasn't close to putting pen to paper on any deal making him New York’s next head coach.
That changed, however, just minutes before midnight once ESPN's Adam Schefter revealed that Harbaugh and the Giants were "working to finalize an agreement," adding: "Barring a setback, a deal is expected."
While there is still a lot of work to be done regrading specific contract numbers, it appears as though Harbaugh is ready and willing to become the Giants' next head coach.
The Giants have done little to hide their interest in Harbaugh ever since he was shown the door by Ravens team owner Steve Bisciotti. Back in November, New York fired Brian Daboll after a 2-8 start in the 2025 campaign.
In their pursuit of Harbaugh, Giants general manager Joe Schoen has maintained frequent contact with the coach while co-owner John Mara has made a direct pitch.
Several of the franchise’s legends have additionally lent a hand, with Tom Coughlin and Eli Manning each speaking to Harbaugh about their time with the Giants.
Even Daboll — who compiled a 20-40-1 record in the Big Apple — spoke highly of New York’s organization and Schoen despite being canned.

While at the Giants’ facility, Harbaugh is also said to have met with quarterback Jaxson Dart, who’s coming off a strong rookie campaign in which he completed 216-of-339 passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions while also rushing 86 times for 487 yards and another nine scores.
It should come as no surprise why the Giants are so determined to land Harbaugh given the immense success he's achieved in the NFL.
During his nearly two-decade tenure with the Ravens, Harbaugh led the team to an impressive 180-113 record and a 13-11 postseason mark, highlighted by a 34-31 victory over the San Francisco 49ers in Super Bowl XLVII.
